headline: Would have canceled an ATF rule on when pistols with attached stabilizing braces count as rifles under federal gun law.
what_it_does: This resolution would have canceled a rule from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) published on January 31, 2023. That rule sets criteria for deciding when a firearm with an attached stabilizing brace that helps it be fired from the shoulder counts as a rifle. Firearms that meet those criteria can fall under the National Firearms Act, which includes requirements such as registration. Under Congress's review process, canceling the rule would also have barred the ATF from issuing a substantially similar rule without new authority from Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Owners of firearms with attached stabilizing braces
who_it_affects.how: They would not have been subject to the rule's criteria that could make their firearms count as rifles requiring registration under the National Firearms Act.
They would not have had to apply the rule's criteria when making or selling firearms with stabilizing braces.

who_it_affects.group: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives
who_it_affects.how: The agency would have lost this rule and could not have issued a substantially similar one without new authority from Congress.
